classification.plan: Read-only filesystem-dependent plan; absolute roots and member Git presence affect output.
classification.refresh: Mutating orchestration with network, toolchain, environment, time and filesystem dependencies; not qualified for reuse.
classification.timer: User-systemd rendering/install/refresh/uninstall with filesystem and service-manager effects; not qualified for reuse.
classification.linkInto: Filesystem mutation exposed through the service; preserves existing nonsymlink paths and refuses a symlinked .repos directory.

inputs: Owner scripts/references.json; HOME; BEEP_REFERENCES_ROOT; explicit root; PATH; jobs; member Git metadata, cleanliness, branch and HEAD.
Git remotes and network results; resolved git/graft binaries; Graft configuration, source trees and deep-provider environment.
Installed systemd owner/root/calendar directives, Bun executable resolution and user unit directory; graft environment-file presence and service environment.
Clock for refresh timestamp; temporary filename generation; child process output and exit status.
findings: Root precedence is explicit flag, nonempty environment override, then home-relative manifest default. Manifest is read even with an explicit root.
Plan checks member .git presence and prints clone/link/build suggestions, but performs no clone. Refresh likewise does not provision missing clones; missing Git metadata becomes pull-failed.

Before cleanliness checks, refresh may append graft exclusions to .git/info/exclude. Dirty/off-main members skip pull and member build; clean main uses pull --ff-only. Workspace build/check still run after member failures or skips.
Deep members use build --deep --allow-partial with jobs and optional directory filters. Structural members use build without deep flags. Production deep builds were not executed by this review.

Child captures are trimmed, bounded to 8 Mi characters and may merge stdout/stderr. This cannot establish exact raw log or byte equality. Maintenance children receive a restricted environment, while deep builds, notify-send and systemctl extend it.

Refresh writes last-refresh.json via a temporary file and rename and may issue a critical notification. Member failures can be encoded in a returned status; the CLI prints that status rather than explicitly converting every failed member into a command error.

Timer rendering includes an environment file, frozen-lockfile pre-install, twelve-hour timeout, persistent scheduling and randomized delay. Install and refresh write units and enable the timer; uninstall disables it and removes units. These are not executed against live workstation units by this review.

Manifest decode rejects excess fields and duplicate member names. Timer fields use the shared SystemdUnitPath schema. Errors retain path, message and optional defect details; output safety is not implied by type validity.

tests.scope: Temporary filesystem fixtures and shell stand-ins for git, graft, notify-send and systemctl; codec/property tests included. No production pulls, paid deep builds or live timer changes.

remaining: The Refs-specific obligation now has bounded source/fixture review; transitive systemd, process, Git and Graft semantics and actual runtime closure remain incomplete.
All 14 census obligations remain attached. No signed remote evidence, task qualification or fresh hosted proof is established.
